learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the invisible pillars of society—family, marriage, religion, economy, and state—and how they keep the human world organized and running!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: An institution is not a building; it is a socially approved system of rules, norms, and procedures that fulfill the basic needs of society. Examples include Family, Education, Religion, and the Economy.

Family is a group of people linked by blood, marriage, or adoption. Families can be Nuclear (parents + children) or Extended (including grandparents/uncles). Kinship refers to the web of social relationships that form family lines.

Marriage establishes a socially recognized family. Monogamy is marriage to one person. Polygamy is marriage to multiple partners. Endogamy is marrying within one's own group (like caste), while Exogamy is marrying outside it.

Economic institutions organize how goods are produced and distributed (e.g., capitalism vs. socialism). Political institutions deal with the distribution of power and authority in society (e.g., the State, democracy).
Sociologists study religion not to prove if God exists, but to see how religious beliefs and rituals create social solidarity (bringing people together) and influence human behavior.

fun_activity.title: 🌳 Map Your Kinship
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a family tree going back to your great-grandparents. Now, highlight who belongs to your 'Patrilineal' side (father's line) and your 'Matrilineal' side (mother's line). Notice the web of kinship!

exam_tips: 📌 Always define 'Institution' as an established set of rules and procedures, NOT a physical building.
📌 Clearly differentiate between 'Endogamy' (marrying inside a group) and 'Exogamy' (marrying outside a group).
📌 Know the difference between Matrilocal (couple lives with bride's family) and Patrilocal (couple lives with groom's family) residence.
quick_recap: ⭐ Institutions constrain individuals (give them rules) but also provide opportunities.
⭐ The family is the most universal and fundamental social institution.
⭐ Education as an institution serves to transmit culture, train the workforce, and socialize the youth.
